Published: 11:36 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:47 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Salford City manager Karl Robinson is in the running for the Bromley job and could be joined in the dugout by a Premier League icon.

Daily Mail Sport understands that former Tottenham striker Jermain Defoe, most recently Woking manager, has been discussed as a potential assistant should Robinson be appointed to fill the vacancy left by Andy Woodman, who was dismissed last month.

Defoe left Woking after less than four months following a breakdown in his relationship with the club's director of football.

His departure came in dramatic circumstances, failing to turn up for training on the eve of the new season before calling the club to say he would not be returning.

Robinson previously tried to sign Defoe on a free transfer after he left Scottish club Rangers while Oxford United manager.

Defoe played 496 Premier League games, spread across six clubs, scoring 163 goals.

Jermain Defoe (right) could return to coaching soon as potential assistant manager of Bromley

He is Tottenham's seventh-highest all-time goalscorer and ranks 10th on the Premier League's all-time scoring list.

Having failed to land Defoe as a player, Robinson could yet get his man in management.

Bromley have been assessing several candidates as their managerial search enters its second week.

They have already held talks with Chelsea legend Ashley Cole, who took charge of Serie B club Cesena for three months at the end of last season, while former Oxford United boss Matt Bloomfield is in the frame. Cole was previously assistant manager of England Under-21s.

The Ravens sit bottom of League One and are winless in six matches.

Woodman was sacked after five years in charge, having led Bromley from the National League to League One, with just two wins in ten matches in their maiden season in the third tier.

Speaking on the Inside the 72 podcast this week, Woodman said: 'You have to speak honestly. The easiest way I can sum this up is that when I got the job at Bromley, my first game was Wealdstone and my last game in the league was Leicester.

'I'm pretty disappointed, pretty upset and feel pretty misled in numerous ways and situations.

Defoe could join former Salford City manager Karl Robinson if he takes over at the club

'To give five and a half years of my life to a club and a fan base that I really loved and bought into and gave everything I had and be told in no less than four minutes, thanks, that was it really.

'There's no other way of dressing this up. I'm disappointed but that's football as we know it. Unfortunately, it never surprises me.'

Byron Webster, who made 173 appearances in six years at Bromley, is currently in interim charge at the south-east London club.

Away from footballing matters, former Everton striker and cult hero Victor Anichebe is in the final stages of completing a takeover at Bromley. Anichebe is understood to be involved in the search for a new manager.

#1920. England squad confirmed: Winners and losers from Thomas Tuchel's selection including Jobe Bellingham, Josh King, Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 13:23, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 10:03

England boss Thomas Tuchel has confirmed his squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

The Three Lions will head into their final two league phase matches in a strong position after taking nine points from their first four games.

Sitting in second spot in Group A3, England are all but guaranteed a quarter-final spot and could still finish above current leaders Spain.

England will return to action against Croatia at Wembley on November 12, before they head to Madrid for a meeting with the world champions on November 16.

Here, Sports Mole assesses the winners and losers of Tuchel's squad ahead of those Nations League fixtures.

Undoubtedly, the names of Jobe Bellingham and Josh King caught the eye when the squad was announced on Friday morning.

Jobe, younger brother of Jude Bellingham, has been a regular fixture at Under-21 level, having made 12 appearances for Lee Carsley's side.

But not many would have predicted his call-up to the senior squad, despite appearing to have taken an extra step in his performance levels with Borussia Dortmund this term.

The 21-year-old has started eight of Dortmund's matches across the Bundesliga and Champions League this term, including a strong display in the Der Klassiker last weekend.

Like Bellingham, King is another player who has earned his first senior call-up after enjoying plenty of football in Carsley's Under-21 side.

The 19-year-old has been one of the first names on Alvaro Arbeloa's team sheet this season, netting two goals and contributing one assist in his nine Premier League appearances.

King primarily plays as a number 10, but Tuchel has revealed he is keen "to see him on both wings" as he weighs up how best to utilise the youngster in his squad.

Ben White, meanwhile, has returned to the England squad for the first time since the March international window, when he was booed by some fans in games against Uruguay and Japan.

Some England supporters were seemingly reluctant to look past White's self-imposed exile from international football after an alleged falling out with Gareth Southgate's assistant Steve Holland at the 2022 World Cup.

After being omitted from the World Cup squad and missing the last international window through injury, White will be hoping to enjoy something of a fresh start when he links up with his England teammates next week.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is also a winner of Tuchel's selection despite struggling for game time at Real Madrid amid competition from Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries.

The former Liverpool man ultimately earned Tuchel's backing with the couple of encouraging performances he produced during the last international window.

Chelsea star Cole Palmer leads the list of notable omissions from Tuchel's 25-man selection for the games against Croatia and Spain.

Palmer, who missed out on selection for the World Cup, withdrew from the last England squad due to a small fitness issue.

At the time, Tuchel expressed his frustration with Palmer's withdrawal, claiming the attacker "misses too many camps".

Tuchel is not short of options for number 10s, and with concerns over Palmer's commitment to the national team, he has decided to pick other players who can provide cover for Jude Bellingham and compete for spots out wide.

The inclusion of Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White, Eberechi Eze and King has also cost Phil Foden a place in the 25-man squad.

Foden has netted four goals and four assists in 11 competitive appearances for Manchester City this term, but he has struggled to deliver at international level and has not been selected since March.

In midfield, Manchester United's Kobbie Mainoo is the main notable omission, with Tuchel opting to hand Jobe his first England call-up instead.

Mainoo was left on the bench for England's World Cup campaign and then withdrew from the last squad with an unspecified injury.

With Tuchel placing importance on attending camps, the reasoning behind Mainoo's exclusion may be similar to Palmer's.

Nico O'Reilly, meanwhile, played the duration of September's defeat to Spain before he withdrew from the squad due to injury.

But he will not be involved this time around after being snubbed in favour of Lewis Hall and Djed Spence.

#1919. Amorim discusses Milan’s consistency, identity and disappointments so far: “We can beat anyone”

Ahead of Thursday’s Europa League game against Ferencvaros, AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

Tomorrow, Milan will be forced to bounce back in Europe with three points. It’s been an up-and-down campaign for them so far, losing to Benfica and Bournemouth, but they grabbed a win against RB Salzburg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A top-eight place is not out of the question, but they will have to be perfect for all of their remaining games in the Europa League league phase. In short, it will not be easy, but it’s not impossible.

Tomorrow, the Portuguese is expected to rotate heavily, offering some of his senior players a chance to rest after a very busy October. For example, Strahinja Pavlovic didn’t train today and isn’t expected to start, either.

Speaking alongside Koni De Winter, Amorim addressed the quality of his opponents, rotations and his assessments of the season so far, as MilanNews relays.

The Derby was a good one, but now it’s behind them. Milan needs consistency…

“This is the objective. The Inter game is over and we need to focus on the Europa League. We were very consistent during the derby, but there were games where we weren’t. This is the big step forward we need to take.

“Rotation doesn’t matter, nor the players we field: we need to be a great team. We need to win tomorrow, because it’s crucial to our goal of going all the way in this competition.”

“First of all, the most important match is the next one. We have to be very careful with some players. We have this busy schedule behind us and we can’t afford to lose many players for the next matches, because sometimes, when you don’t want to rotate your squad, you end up with an injury that keeps you out for a month or a month and a half.

“This is the most important match; we’re only thinking about it, but we’ll have to rotate a bit, and all the players are ready to handle the impact of the demands of the game. We have the desire to win the match.

“We’ll be facing a great opponent who has nine points in this competition, a team that hasn’t lost a single game in the league, but our players are ready, and we have a duty to win.”

Why this difference between Serie A and the Europa League?

“But if you look at the games against Benfica, I think we didn’t play our best, despite having more possession. We had some problems with the few chances we gave the opponent, and we conceded goals.

“Then we won a great game in Salzburg and then in Bournemouth. We had a red card, two penalties, and it was our fault. Maignan’s situation didn’t help us fight for the game, and sometimes these dynamics happen at certain times.

“I think we’re not doing very well in Serie A; obviously, we won the last one, but looking at the team and the games, I think we should have more points. So I’m not satisfied in the Europa League, I’m not satisfied in Serie A.

“I think we can do better, but that’s how it goes sometimes. Every game has its own story. But I think we can do better tomorrow and win.”

“They’re a team that’s used to winning, no matter the context. It gives you full confidence in every game. They’re comfortable. They’re doing very well in the league. They play a 4-2-3-1 formation and have a strong identity.

“In midfield, Nagy is very good at building play. They’re comfortable; they come to San Siro with nothing to lose. The responsibility at San Siro is ours: we have to play well and stay focused.

“I told the players that against Inter we did well because we remained humble and attentive to detail: against Ferencvaros, we’ll have to do the same because they’re a very strong team.”

After the Europa League draw, Antonio Cassano said that Milan and Juventus cannot take victory against Ferencvaros for granted…

“Without a doubt. We’re capable of winning every match and losing every match. It depends on our approach, regardless of the opponent. Everyone knows everyone; every player has the tools to understand, and the coaches have the tools to prepare everything as best as possible.

“We can win and lose against anyone; it’s all up to us. And sometimes you also need a little bit of luck.”

Does your AC Milan already have a clear identity? Are we far off?

You often ask me when we’ll reach the top. We’ll never reach the top, even if we win every game. We always have to improve. We already have an identity: we want to dominate games, sometimes we manage to do it, sometimes we don’t.

“Sometimes we change the formation and the defensive phase and nobody even notices. Our identity is to be proactive: we still lack the ability to put opponents in the box to create more chances.

“But we’re playing better, we even manage certain moments better. But there’s still a lot of work to do, especially in the final 30 meters: I have to help my players do that.

On the excellent defensive phase against Inter:

“Inter are a thing of the past. We can show tomorrow that we can defend better. We defended, but with the ball. It allowed us to think better. Details are important: a meter is a meter. We were better than Bologna.

“We were very aggressive on the wings. Koni was exceptional, but if a cross comes in for Thuram, it’s very difficult to defend, so we were more aggressive without the ball to avoid crosses. We have to do the same tomorrow; they are used to winning games.

“When a team consistently wins, there must be a reason, and we have to be ready for tomorrow.”

“We have to give him credit; he’s working really well. He went through a period without playing and was a bit frustrated, but he’s always worked very well. I think he can play this role on the wing. We played with Moreira there once, but against Inter it was Diawara. Same role, different interpretation.

“During the break, against Padova, we tried him at left back: he showed important signs. He’s quick, he’s strong. He’s doing well, he has the potential to improve a lot. Against Inter, we knew how dangerous crosses could be, especially from Inter’s left flank.

“Dimarco didn’t play, but the tactical idea remained the same, and defending crosses with Koni and Pavlovic proved to be a good idea. They almost scored from a cross with Calhanoglu, but I think he’s doing really well.

“He has plenty of room for improvement, and who knows, maybe he’ll start tomorrow.”

“What I was saying about winning games, this is the team’s strength, our identity. I always put the team first, not the individual, even though we have excellent individual players. The Ferencvaros striker is very strong in space: he can play both as a winger and as a forward, and I think he’ll play as a striker against us.

“Nagy is an important player because he understands the game. He knows exactly when to drop back and when to stay high, and I really like that kind of player.

“Add to this the quality of the left-back with his right foot who can cut inside: all these little details define an identity that I really appreciate in this team, and we’ll have to be ready to process all this information to prepare and win the match.

“I repeat: we have three points in this competition and we absolutely must win tomorrow.”

It was the best second half of the entire championship, the one against Inter. I saw the attitude of a great team: authoritative, confident, without taking risks. Should we start again from the second half?

“I think it’s a good point. But you can’t separate the second half from the first; they’re connected. We took the lead in the first half, then we controlled the game that way in the second half. We improved our understanding of the game; we were complete in all areas.

“Maybe we were lacking in putting a few players behind Inter’s midfield: we had good possession, but we can do even better. It’s just one game, anyway. But thinking only about the derby is a small-team mentality: every game is important to us.

“Tomorrow I’ll understand my team better than the derby. I don’t care about the Inter game anymore. Was it nice to win? Yes. But I’m still angry about the Bologna game. Tomorrow we’ll have to be strong to win.”

The Derby showed a side of Cardinale emotional… When will we see her like this too?

“When we win the Scudetto or a major title, maybe I’ll be excited. Until then, it’s just another day. But I didn’t expect to feel this way during the match, and neither did Cardinale. He gave an important interview, saying he supports the coach.

“There was a wonderful feeling in the stadium; he enjoyed this moment and was emotional. He’s American, but when you spend time here, you become a little Italian. However, I won’t be excited until I win something. And when I do win something, I’ll already be thinking about the next Scudetto. I doubt you’ll see me emotional.”

#1917. Why Unai Emery is right to turn down Manchester United and stick with Aston Villa

It’s a great quirk of Premier League scheduling that Manchester United welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford this weekend, after a week in which Jamie Carragher’s suggestion that Villa manager Unai Emery would jump at the chance to move to United prompted a legal threat from the midlands club, an apology from the outspoken pundit and an announcement late on Wednesday that Emery and his bosses had ‘positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club’.

A new contract is reportedly imminent for the Spaniard, and who could possibly blame Emery for sticking around at a club that have repeatedly backed him, given him more control than he’ll have anywhere else and whose fans worship him for delivering their first trophy in 30 years last season.

The alternative? Joining a constant catastrophe that everyone agrees needs far more than just a new manager to put back together.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

While Emery is going nowhere, the whole affair does raise questions about football’s food chain, something which definitely does exist but is clearly going through some changes right now.

Managers will always believe they are the right person to take a once great club and bring back the glory days, and being the one to do so is an intoxicating idea.

But Emery has been here before and was burned by his experience at Arsenal where a collection of expensive failed transfers and unmotivated senior players gave him the worst possible platform to build from. Sound familiar?

All roads still lead to Real Madrid for players but the money involved in Premier League football means simply being a relatively successful English club puts you closer to the top of the chain than ever before, and given United’s penchant for finding new lows every season, a move from Villa north to Manchester is at best a sideways move these days – just ask Youri Tielemans.

Also, given the relative state of flux that many of the ‘big six’ find themselves in these days, there’s an opportunity for Emery and Villa to elbow their way in and become a more established fixture towards the top of the league.

Select your team for football news tailored to you Close

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United are joined by Spurs in their ability to self-implode, Chelsea are chaotic at the best of times, Liverpool are still just about managing the transition to a Jurgen Klopp-less existence and Manchester City are unlikely to be challenging for titles in the near future, depending on impending sanctions.

Only Arsenal are properly set up for consistent success, and Villa clearly believe trusting in Emery is the best way to eventually get themselves into the title conversation.

There are pitfalls to their approach – if Emery does someday get his head turned by a massive paycheck in Saudi Arabia or Real Madrid do come calling, he may still move on and leave the club as a ship without a sail, which is why clubs like Brighton and Brentford treat their managers as cogs in a well-oiled system.

United fans had some temporary relief midweek with their emotional comeback against Roma in the Champions League and may well go into the international break feeling good if they manage to squeeze out a win on Sunday, but regardless of the result, Emery is in the right place.

#1915. Arsenal urged to avoid £64m transfer mistake after Micah Richards claim

Arsenal should be wary of selling Viktor Gyokeres in the January transfer window, according to former Gunners striker Jeremie Aliadiere.

Gyokeres produced his best performance of the season in midweek with a goal and an assist to help the Gunners beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the Champions League.

But it has otherwise proved to be a frustrating few months for the Swede, who has started just one Premier League match for Mikel Arteta’s side so far this season.

Gyokeres amassed a respectable 21 goals in all competitions in his maiden season after arriving from Sporting CP for £64million, but now faces an uncertain future at the Emirates having fallen beneath Kai Havertz in the pecking order.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

With speculation likely to mount ahead of the January window, some pundits, including Micah Richards, have suggested that the Gunners should look to move Gyokeres on.

But former Arsenal striker Aliadiere believes that might be a mistake and ultimately leave Arteta short of options at the top of the pitch.

‘I think it’s all depending on the finances how much they can get for him and who to replace him with,’ Aliadiere told Metro.

‘Because I think as much as obviously he’s not in the top 11 now because Havertz is preferred number one, you don’t want to sell him, get a good price and not be able to replace him.

‘If Havertz gets injured, which obviously we’ve seen in the past – he’s had a few injuries and he can pick up injuries – you just end up with no striker at all.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So I think it’s a very difficult January transfer window. Do you try to buy someone before you sell? I think when you look over the summer, selling Trossard and Martinelli before buying somebody.

‘Obviously, they go to Tzolis, but I’m not sure Tzolis was bought to be the first choice and when he is injured, you end up doing Eze on the left-hand side, and that’s not really his best position in my opinion.

‘So I don’t want it to happen with Gyokeres, thinking let’s try to sell him and recuperate a good transfer fee for him and then not replacing him.’

But even if Gyokeres remains at the club, Aliadiere can’t envisage the 28-year-old becoming the long-term solution to Arsenal’s search for a clinical striker.

‘I just feel the way Arsenal plays does not quite suit Gyokeres’ style of play,’ Aliadiere, speaking via football betting, added.

‘I’ve always been very quite patient and looking at the good stuff that he does, and I still feel that he does some amazing work. But I just do feel that the players don’t really give him the ball quick enough, which is what he needs.

‘He needs to be on 1v1. He needs to run the channel, get fed the ball quite quickly. And I feel we’re not really playing that way. We like to control the ball.

‘We like to control the tempo and just slow down the game. And I just feel Gyokeres is more of a counter-attacking player where he sees the space, he wants it quickly and then he’s on 1v1 and then he can then dominate physically.

‘But he’s rarely getting in that position, so I just find it difficult to kind of see him turning things around in a way of probably just being a rotation player.’

#1914. Genoa vs AC Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 13:24, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 13:27

After a week of highs and lows, AC Milan will head towards the international break with a tough trip to Genoa on Sunday afternoon.

Before they clash at Stadio Ferraris, the hosts have actually claimed more points from their last five Serie A games than the inconsistent Rossoneri.

From derby delight to Europa League debacle, Milan have enjoyed and endured an eventful few days.

Soon after Ruben Amorim's unbeaten domestic record was ended by Bologna, his side entered the Derby della Madonnina as underdogs against reigning champions Inter Milan.

Yet, the Rossoneri surged into a two-goal lead through Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic, before Diego Moreira's free-kick sealed an impressive win - their sixth in eight games against Inter.

Having closed within four points of their city rivals, Milan sit fifth in Serie A and could be contenders for the title - but that good feeling did not last for long.

Beaten for a third time in four Europa League fixtures, they went down 2-0 to Ferencvaros on Thursday night and may be facing an early exit.

It was also a rare failure to find the net, as Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 league games under Amorim - the best record of any new coach since club legend Cesare Maldini back in 1972.

The Rossoneri also remain undefeated on their travels around Italy - recording two wins and three draws so far - and they usually get the right result in Genoa.

Including a 2-1 victory at the very end of last term, Milan have won four straight away games against Sunday's hosts.

In fact, Genoa have won none of the last 10 league meetings, either home or away - a drought dating back to March 2020.

The Rossoblu may fancy putting a halt to that long winless run, having just ended their eight-year wait for three consecutive Serie A victories.

Much has changed since Daniele De Rossi swerved the sack during the last international break, as four wins from five have propelled his side up the standings.

Potentially facing a change of management and another relegation fight, they instead conjured up a stunning run of results.

Now occupying 11th place, Genoa continued their rise with a 2-1 win at Lecce last week, when ex-Milan man Junior Messias set up the opener before netting the second himself.

It has been 17 years since the Grifone posted four straight wins in a single top-flight campaign, but such a streak is now on the cards.

Three days on from a dismal defeat to Ferencvaros, it is likely that Amorim will make multiple changes.

For sure, Milan captain Mike Maignan will replace Lorenzo Torriani in goal, after serving a Europa League suspension on Thursday.

After his derby heroics, Moreira was initially benched in midweek, but he could also return to the starting XI; the Belgian winger has racked up seven goal involvements from his first six Serie A appearances.

Though Strahinja Pavlovic should be brought back after a fitness issue, Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Mattia Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek are still unavailable.

By contrast, Genoa boss De Rossi may have a full squad to choose from, as Elias Havel and Lorenzo Venturino recently returned from long layoffs.

Milutin Osmajic is the hosts' top scorer with four league goals, while ex-Milan forward Stephan El Shaarawy seems to be returning to form.

The former Italy international - who made 83 appearances and scored 21 times for the Rossoneri in Serie A - has provided an assist in both of his last two games.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Frendrup, Traore, Ellertsson; Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos

Allied to two cup wins at Stadio Ferraris, Genoa have won half of their first six home games in Serie A, so Milan will be put through a stern test.

While Amorim's men are leaking too many goals, De Rossi's side have found their shooting boots, and that could produce an end-to-end draw.

#1911. Leeds United 1 Spurs 0: Okafor the hero as intense, in-character second half ends winless streak

Shortly after being serenaded after coming on in the final quarter at Elland Road, he took care of Spurs in the here and now.

The fact that three substitutes all combined will not have been missed by Daniel Farke, who misses nothing.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A throw-in from Melvin Bard was won by Dominic Calvert-Lewin with the ball dropping to Harry Wilson, who had the presence of mind to spot Okafor, who gave Rodrigo Bentacur the slip before firing home confidently on 77 minutes.

And that was that as Leeds produced an intense, in-character second half to secure a first win in six matches and head into the international break in improved mood. A fourth win in a row for the first time in over 1,000 days continues for Spurs.

The win was not without controversy, that said.

It took a big moment on 37 minutes to set pulses truly racing among home punters in an otherwise pretty uneventful first half.

A lengthy VAR check saw the Stockley Park overlords scrutinise Jayden Bogle’s challenge on Mathys Tel for a considerable length of time before it was deemed not to be serious foul play.

Tel was left writhing in agony after being caught on the back of his Achilles by Bogle’s left foot. It looked accidental as opposed to intentional and the video decision-makers concurred, although it could easily have gone the other way and resulted in a red card.

Tel managed to carry on for a few minutes before eventually making way.

The other incident of note also involved technology with an early check resulting in a non-penalty award for Leeds after a cross caught Mateus Fernandes’ shoulder. The Spurs midfielder’s arm was outstretched, but it was rightly deemed as not intentional.

Headline team news from a home perspective saw Lucas Nmecha and Longstaff handed first league starts of the campaign, with Harry Wilson and Dan James dropping to the bench.

You had to go back to last November for the previous time that Longstaff stepped out from the off at Premier League level.

Spurs-wise, ex-United favourite Archie Gray switched to midfield following the recall of Pedro Porro at right-back.

Gray received a few jeers whenever he touched the ball. Spurs had some half-decent moments in transition and had the better of it in open play and more control - with Fernandes seeing plenty of the ball in particular. Leeds displayed perspiration, but little inspiration.

Spurs’ best moments arrived midway through the half. An incisive move down Leeds’ right ended in Omar Marmoush’s low shot taking a slight, but important touch off Tarik Muharemovic before James Trafford gathered. The deflection took the sting out of it.

Mohammed Kudus also tested Trafford low down, with the Leeds keeper having no first-half dramas unlike seven days earlier.

Leeds, who started nicely enough, huffed and puffed. One chance arrived ahead of the break but Nmecha’s downward header was easily claimed by Antonin Kinsky.

Leeds made a change at the interval, with Melvin Bard coming on for Gabriel Gudmundsson, presumably due to an injury concern.

Attacking the Kop, Leeds produced a dangerous moment with Van de Ven getting a key clearance in front of goal after Bogle whipped in an excellent low centre.

Longstaff’s left-wing corner yielded the hosts best moment up to press.

Calvert-Lewin directed a header towards goal and Dominic Solanke got an important block. The Leeds striker helped the ball back into the danger zone, with Nico Elvedi nodding wide.

United, attacking the Kop, were starting to up it and soon missed a golden chance after Tanaka and Longstaff led the break.

Calvert-Lewin did well to evade van der Veen and teed up Tanaka, who ballooned an excellent chance over.

Nevertheless, Leeds were the ones in the ascendancy and Spurs were starting to look flustered all of a sudden. Indicative of that was a triple change just before the midway point of the half from Roberto De Zerbi.

One flash of life - in relative isolation -from the visitors saw one of the substitutes in Conor Gallagher fire a shot just wide. Most of the action was towards the other end. Nmecha hit a post, but the flag was instantly raised before Calvert-Lewin fired over, soon followed by Bogle.

Leeds continued to knock on the door, with Kinsky forced into significant work to tip over Longstaff’s hooked effort in splendid fashion.

The pressure was sustained and the Kop sucked one in. Trafford made a key late save to deny Van Hecke.

Leeds United: Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle (Rodon 93), Ampadu, Longstaff (Greuv 93), Tanaka (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson (Bard HT); Nmecha (Okafor 77), Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes unused: Zetterer, James, Aaronson, Bijol.

Published: 18:02 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EDT, 3 November 2026

Michael Carrick and Manchester United are enduring the club's worst start to a league season in 40 years, with the Red Devils languishing in 17th place.

Their woes in recent years have been well documented, with the club seemingly incapable of finding anyone to match the glory days under Sir Alex Ferguson.

Since his departure in 2013, they have had eight managers – seven of whom have managed them in Europe's biggest competition.

The three-time champions of Europe have performed particularly poorly in the Champions League in that time, not making it past the quarter-finals once in seven attempts.

They have won less than half of their Champions League fixtures since Ferguson left – and only 34 per cent in the current decade.

Carrick brought United back into the Champions League last season but since being given the permanent role has hit shocking form

And they will be lucky to even reach that stage this season if they continue to play as they have been in the competition, losing to Atletico Madrid away and being embarrassed by Champions League debutants Como.

With United set to take on Roma on Tuesday in their fourth game of the competition, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at how each manager on United's carousel has fared in the Champions League... and where it unravelled for all of them.

It feels as if it has been an age since David Moyes took the reins at Old Trafford. The Scotsman had a torrid time in his ten-month spell at United.

His tenure was characterised by embarrassing losses, a lack of consistency and an inability to transition from the old regime.

Moyes was sacked in April after a 2-0 loss to his old Everton side that ended United's hopes of a top-four finish for that season. He was already under serious pressure having been dumped out of the Champions League in the quarter-finals by Bayern Munich.

Moyes was handpicked by Ferguson to replace him but didn't even last a season at United

The current Everton manager oversaw a 1-1 draw at home in the first leg, with Nemanja Vidic's goal being cancelled out by Bastian Schweinsteiger – who moved to Old Trafford a year later. But Bayern – managed by Pep Guardiola – quickly responded to Patrice Evra's goal in the second leg to win it 3-1.

They had to battle to even get that far, with a comfortable group stage – four wins and two draws – being followed by an embarrassing 2-0 defeat at Olympiacos in the first leg of the last 16. A Robin van Persie hat-trick in the second leg spared their blushes.

The big Dutchman came to United with a stellar CV having won both the Champions League and UEFA Cup with Ajax in the 90s, as well as league titles in Spain and Germany.

And he seemed the exact kind of serial winner who would be the perfect replacement for Ferguson, but it just didn't work out. Van Gaal spent heavily in the market when he arrived - most notably breaking the British transfer record to secure the services of Angel Di Maria for £59.7million - but he simply couldn't find his feet in England.

Van Gaal had just the one season in the Champions League with United before leaving, and it was possibly the most disastrous since Ferguson's departure.

They were placed in a group with Wolfsburg, PSV and CSKA Moscow, and were dumped out at the earliest possible stage, finishing third in the group with just eight points. They fell into the Europa League and - after overturning a disastrous 2-1 defeat by Danish side Midtjylland in the first leg of their last-32 game - were sent packing by Liverpool.

Joining in 2016 after being sacked by Chelsea, Jose Mourinho immediately got busy in the market.

And initially it seemed as if he was going to make it work. Paul Pogba and Zlatan Ibrahimovic arrived and United won their first three games. Although their league form dipped, they did go on to win the League Cup and the Europa League in that first season.

But then it all began to fall away. Like Van Gaal and Moyes before him, Mourinho only got one try at his favourite competition with United, and exited in a less than graceful manner.

Jose won the Europa League whilst in Manchester but never really found success in the big competition

He may have won it with Porto in 2004 and Inter six years later but at United he only got as far as the round of 16, and crashed out after a 2-1 home defeat by Sevilla following a 0-0 draw in the first leg.

Recently Jose revealed that his relationship with the Red Devils was very nearly different. In his new Netflix biopic, Mourinho, he said that he had agreed to take over straight after Ferguson - only to be lured back to Chelsea by Roman Abramovich instead. Who knows how he would have fared at Old Trafford if he had joined three years earlier.

Mourinho's successor also had an excellent start to life in the United dugout but ended up being hounded out after a tumultuous three years.

When Ole was at the wheel, at first it seemed like United were on course to return to the big time however, slowly but surely, it became clear that it wasn't going to work out.

Solskjaer is one of two men on this list to have won the Champions League with United as a player and the Norwegian scored arguably the most historic goal in United's European history, getting the dramatic winner in the 1999 final.

And he is probably the only gaffer since Ferguson to have had a positive memorable moment in the competition. It came in Paris in March of 2019, shortly after he took over. After losing 2-0 at home in the first leg of the tie they looked like they were already out but miraculously Ole masterminded a 3-1 victory and won on away goals.

Unfortunately that is where the good times as a manager in the Champions League end. After the PSG win United were beaten 4-0 on aggregate by Barcelona and then didn't make it into the competition for the 2019-20 season.

They did return with Ole in 2020-21 - only to be knocked out in the group stage, finishing third in a group with PSG, RB Leipzig and Turkish side Basaksehir. They went on to reach the Europa League final that year - losing to Villarreal on penalties - and Solskjaer was gone in November, before the end of next season's group stage.

Taking over as interim manager until the end of the 2021-22 campaign - following a caretaker spell from a certain Michael Carrick - Austrian Rangnick was in charge for just three European games.

The final game of the group stage saw a 1-1 draw with Swiss side Young Boys, with Mason Greenwood scoring United's goal.

Then they took on Atletico Madrid in the last-16, and after a 1-1 draw away, were sent packing with a 1-0 second-leg defeat at Old Trafford.

Renan Lodi's header for Atletico Madrid sent United crashing out under Ralf Rangnick

Rangnick's spell at United is best remembered for his forthright assessments of the club's dire situation, and he famously likened their situation to that of a patient needing open-heart surgery.

'You don’t even need glasses to see and analyse where the problems are,' he said. 'Now it’s about how do we solve them? It’s not enough to do some minor amendments. In medicine you would say that this is an operation of the open heart.

'If this happens and everyone has realised that this has to happen and if people want to work together then it makes sense and I believe it doesn’t take two or three years to change those things. This can happen within one year.'

More than four years on, the fans are still waiting.

Erik ten Hag came in nine years after Ferguson's exit, and while he brought a League Cup and an FA Cup to Old Trafford it was not enough to stop him being sacked.

Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League. He actually fared even worse than his predecessors by finishing rock bottom of the group in the 2023-24 season, after particularly rough losses away to Copenhagen and Galatasaray.

Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League

After a dismal eighth-placed finish in the Premier League the FA Cup win over Manchester City ended that season on a high - and saved Ten Hag's job.

He even signed a contract extension that summer, but was ditched by October with United 14th.

Ruben Amorim, who replaced Ten Hag, did not manage United in the Champions League - though he did reach the Europa League final with them in 2025.

His sacking in January this year paved the way for Michael Carrick to join as interim and, in steering them to third place, ensured United were back at Europe's top table after two seasons away.

That also won him the permanent role, but Carrick has had a torrid start to the new campaign - winning just two of his side's 13 games in all competitions and setting a new club record for the longest winless streak in the Premier League era (nine).

One of those wins was in the Champions League against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah, but they followed that with the defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como.

Carrick will hope United can finally arrest this run of form at home to Roma on Tuesday, but it will not be easy with the Italians enjoying an excellent start to the season and currently sitting third in Serie A.

A win, however, could keep Carrick in a job and breathe some life into a United team that desperately needs it.

#1907. De Winter discusses clean sheet chances, relationship with Pavlovic and starting role: “I feel good”

Today, Koni De Winter sat alongside Ruben Amorim for a press conference ahead of AC Milan vs. Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

It’s been a big year for De Winter, with the Belgian going from strength to strength. After the Supercoppa Italiana game against Napoli, the defender has seemingly improved constantly,  even becoming something of a regular for Massimiliano Allegri towards the tail end of last season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, Ruben Amorim has relied on him this season. So far, he’s played in every game of the campaign, and whilst the defence has been hampered by injuries around him, he’s been an ever-present option for the Portuguese.

After the birth of his child today, he was celebrated by the team at Milanello, and he will hope to make a strong week – after the derby win, too – an even better one, with a win tomorrow.

Speaking alongside Amorim, De Winter answered several questions from the media, as MilanNews relays.

This year you became a regular for AC Milan and now you’ve also become a father…

“Becoming a dad is a wonderful thing. On the pitch, I feel more important than last year and I feel more confident. I think it’s a great moment, but there’s still a long way to go.”

You’ve played pretty much all the time so far. Did you expect that?

“I feel good. When there are a lot of games, you train by playing. For me, it’s better this way. So for me, it’s fine like this; I have to be ready.”

You almost always play alongside Pavlovic. How do you get along with the Serbian?

“I feel good with all my teammates; we know each other well. I like playing with Pavlovic; he’s strong and we understand each other very well.”

How difficult will it be to keep a clean sheet tomorrow?

“They’re a good team, they’re having a good Europa League, they have great confidence, but we’ll do our best to stop them from scoring.”

Milan has had many great defenders. Do you have any role models?

“I have several. If I have to name one who played for AC Milan, I’d say Thiago Silva, whom I followed a lot and who is very good. If I have to name one, I’d say his.”

“As the coach says, he’s someone who works hard and always gives his all. Everyone loves him. When you work hard, your chance comes, and he grabbed it with both hands. We’re all happy for him.”

#1906. Nico O'Reilly update: England omission explained and why it benefits all parties including Man City

By Oliver Thomas | 06 Nov 2026 13:27

Nico O'Reilly has been left out of the latest England squad due to fitness-related issues, Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel and Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca have confirmed.

The 22-year-old was selected as England’s first-choice left-back for the 2026 World Cup and helped the Three Lions progress to the semi-finals in North America.

O’Reilly has earned 13 senior caps for England and has featured regularly under Tuchel, but a disrupted period at club level with Man City has led to his omission for November’s international break.

A midfielder by trade who has morphed into a left-back, O’Reilly has played the full 90 minutes just twice for Man City this season and has started seven games out of 15 in all competitions.

O’Reilly has predominantly been dealing with a persistent back problem that he sustained at the beginning of September, while a knee issue has also been causing him some discomfort.

Following England’s squad announcement on Friday morning, Tuchel discussed his full-back options ahead of UEFA Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain, and explained why O’Reilly will not be involved.

Inter Milan’s Djed Spence has returned to the senior fold at the expense of O’Reilly, while Lewis Hall and Jarrad Branthwaite are two other left-footed defensive options called up by Tuchel.

Meanwhile, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarell Quansah and Ben White are all set to battle for starts at right-back, with the latter returning to the Three Lions squad after an eight-month absence.

"Djed [Spence] is on the left side, we left Nico out because he's not fully, fully fit and needs to take his time to get fully fit and take care of his knee,” Tuchel told reporters.

"[Alexander-Arnold] was very good in the last camp, very good in the matches he played. Competition is on and he competes with Jarell and Ben for the position of right full-back."

Speaking at a press conference on Friday ahead of Man City’s Premier League trip to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Maresca also shared his thoughts on O’Reilly’s fitness and his England omission.

"With Nico it's quite easy, some more problems, unfortunately. He's not 100%,” said the Citizens boss.

"In the last game (against RB Leipzig on Wednesday). I really liked him; I think he was playing a very good game, and this is what we need from Nico. Keep him fit because we know how good he is, and no doubt that in the future he will again be with the international team."

Asked whether O'Reilly needed rest over the international break, Maresca replied: "It’s what he needs, to use that break to do the right things in terms of therapy and this kind of things and be 100% over the international break”

O’Reilly’s absence from the England squad may well prove to be a blessing in disguise, as a much-needed break offers the youngster a crucial window to focus entirely on his recovery and return to full fitness.

Rather than risking a further setback on the international stage, the hiatus allows the starlet to build up his sharpness in a controlled environment, ensuring he is fully prepared for the gruelling club football schedule awaiting Man City.

With Maresca’s side facing a notoriously busy winter fixture list – 11 games before the end of the year – having a rejuvenated O'Reilly fresh and ready for domestic duties will provide a massive boost to the Citizens' squad depth.

Furthermore, his omission serves a dual purpose internationally, granting Tuchel the perfect opportunity to assess alternative left-back options and experiment with England's defensive depth in the closing stages of their Nations League group-stage campaign.

Hall is the most likely candidate to start at least one of England’s matches against Croatia and Spain this month, while Spence and Branthwaite provide alternative left-sided cover.

It remains to be seen whether O'Reilly will be involved against Nottingham Forest this weekend, or if he will instead return to action on November 21 when Man City take on Fulham in their first Premier League fixture after the international break.

#1905. Man Utd suffer blow as Michael Carrick reveals how long Carlos Baleba is out for

Manchester United Carlos Baleba is not expected to return until December at the earliest after suffering a hamstring injury.

The summer signing was forced off early in the second-half of Tuesday’s Champions League game against Roma.

The former Brighton star made a bursting run into the box but pulled up just as he was about to pull the trigger on goal.

Baleba appeared to be in tears as he limped off the Old Trafford pitch. Having already missed the opening five games of the campaign as a result of an ankle injury he suffered during pre-season with Brighton, he now faces another spell on the sidelines.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Providing an update in his pre-match press conference ahead of the visit of Aston Villa on Sunday, Carrick confirmed Baleba will be sidelined for the duration of the international break which begins after this weekend’s fixtures.

‘We don’t know exactly, but it’ll be a number of weeks,” Carrick said when asked about the severity of Baleba’s injury.

‘It’s definitely not this week and it won’t be any time over the international break. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.’

In addition to the Villa game, Carrick’s comments suggest Baleba will miss United’s first game back after the international break – away to Liverpool on 22 November.

They are on the road again three days later in a crucial Champions League game against Sporting CP before seeing out the month at home to Newcastle.

#1904. Daniel Farke on 'spot-on' Leeds United, Noah Okafor admission, Gabriel Gudmundsson update + on Spurs controversy

An outstanding second half culminated in a deserved winner in the 77th minute from substitute Noah Okafor, with fellow replacements Harry Wilson and Melvin Bard also contributing to the goal. Okafor scored with his second touch.

It was a merited three points for Leeds, who mustered 13 goal attempts on the restart.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Farke said: "There's no replacement for this winning feeling after such a game in the dressing room. It's great to have this winning feeling back.

"All the credit and all my compliments go to the boys' terrific performance against a really in-form Tottenham side.

"You could see in the first half that they would go with confidence also into this game. For us, of course, a difficult period because we're missing - since a few weeks more or less - in training and also in the starting line-ups, some key players like Anton Stach, Noah Okafor and for Dominic (Calvert-Lewin). It’s not the easiest spell with several injury problems.

"It was important today to show this unity and commitment. We were technically spot on in order to avoid all their processes and all their individual quality in order to score goals and reduce them to very, very little already in the first half.

"We were missing a bit in our game (in the first half) in our final third was again the quality of the crosses and the finishing pass was perhaps not there, but I think in the second half there was no doubt just one team was pushing."

On the impact of Okafor, who had been struggling with an abductor issue, he continued: "Credit to our medical department and also to Noah, he has worked in a very, very disciplined fashion, 24 hours a day more or less to be available.

"Yesterday with a few concerns of the medical department, they said: 'Boss, Listen, if you want to use him, you have to make sure that you stay unbelievably disciplined and you can't bring him on longer than 15 or 20 minutes, this is what the muscle can't handle (more minutes). But if you want to do this and Noah feels also right, then yeah, perhaps you can do this.' He took part yesterday in parts of our team training."

Farke confirmed that Swedish international Gabriel Gudmundsson came off with a hamstring injury at the break, with Bard coming on and performing excellently in his place.

He said: "Gaby had problems with his hamstring, so it was not possible for him to keep going. I always prefer to have Gabby available but don't get me wrong, but I had a good feeling straight away because Melvin had his best week in training since he was together with us.

"He could feel that he has momentum and I was not for one moment concerned when I had to throw him in. I hope that it's not too bad with Gaby and I hope to have him back on the other side of the international break, but also credit for Melvin.

The win was not without controversy, that said.

It took a big moment on 37 minutes to set pulses truly racing among home punters in an otherwise pretty uneventful first half.

A lengthy VAR check saw the Stockley Park overlords scrutinise Jayden Bogle’s challenge on Mathys Tel for a considerable length of time before it was deemed not to be serious foul play.

Tel was left writhing in agony after being caught on the back of his Achilles by Bogle’s left foot. It looked accidental as opposed to intentional and the video decision-makers concurred, although it could easily have gone the other way and resulted in a red card.

Tel managed to carry on for a few minutes before eventually making way. He left the stadium on crutches after the game.

Farke said: "I haven't watched the scenes back and didn't have the chance, so for that I can't give a clear opinion on it. I would need to watch it back. The scene with Jayden was not too far away from my bench, I think it looked a bit like a very unlucky coming together.

"Of course sadly for Mathys that he was injured, and of course fingers crossed that he's back pretty soon. But it felt a bit like there was not too much speed in this action, and what I can guarantee is Jayden Bogle is one of the most fair players in the whole country.

"He's too much sometimes for me like a butterfly and not like an eagle anyhow, so soft in a positive way. What I can guarantee is that he would never ever injure a player on purpose, or not even foul a player on purpose, because he's a great character."

Spurs chief Roberto De Zerbi had no complaints about the result and felt his side's second-half performance lacked 'personality'.

He said: "It was two games in the same game. In the first half, we had clear chances to score and didn't suffer.

"In the second half, I don't know why, we suffered too much and deserved to lose game. We didn't win any duels and one-on-one's. There was space to play, but we didn't take the right positions and didn't show personality and who we are.

"I don't want excuses. We have to be honest, if we are not honest today, the future is not good. I was surprised as my players worked very well this week. We spoke all week about the intensity and type of game we would find in this stadium. It was not a surprise for us."

On the incident regarding Tel, he added: "I can't say something more because I didn't clearly see the situation.

"I was surprised, because in the same position in the second half, there were two different fouls and two yellow cards (offences) on Pedro Porro.

"I don't know if it was a red card or not on Mathys Tel, but for sure Pedro Porro, it was a yellow card. Why I'm telling it like this, because the parameter of the referee was not good enough, I think, for these both situations."

Former England Lioness Mary Earps has revealed the birth of a ‘secret’ baby boy with her partner Kitty Forrest.

At the end of the video, Earps revealed that ‘Baby Forrest Earps’ was born on November 5.

#1902. Barnsley FC 7 Aldershot Town 2: League One strugglers cruise into second round of FA Cup

Barnsley cruised into the second round of the FA Cup with an emphatic 7-2 win over Aldershot Town.

The fifth-tier Shots were ruthlessly dismantled by the third-tier Reds, who were clinical in front of a sparse Oakwell crowd.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Captain Cameron McGeehan stole the show with a hat-trick, while Vimal Yoganathan notched a brace and Reyes Cleary and Rylan Brownlie got in on the act.

Aldershot did give their travelling supporters something to celebrate late on when Annisuis Lewis struck twice, but they were merely consolations.

The game followed the natural order of cup ties when there is a division gap from the get-go, with the higher-ranked team enjoying the lion’s share of possession.

Ziyad Larkeche was the first to penetrate the Aldershot box, receiving a pass from Cleary on the overlap and fizzing a cross towards McGeehan. The cross was drilled at Barnsley’s captain rather than to him, therefore the midfielder could only bundle harmlessly wide.

Barnsley did have the ball in the back of the net early on, when McGeehan was sent through by Daniel Johnson and rolled it into the bottom corner, only for the offside flag to appear.

Aldershot were not dealing with an onslaught but there continued to be a steady flow of promising ventures forward by the hosts. A tidy swivel from Luca Connell in the middle of the park quickly shifted into attack and he picked out Tobi Adeyemo, who saw a tame shot held comfortably by Nick Hayes.

Aldershot’s goalkeeper, however, could not get to a McGeehan header sent towards the top corner after a peach of a delivery from Jubril Okedina.

Barnsley’s feet remained firmly pressed on the gas and the lead was doubled less than 10 minutes later. A Yoganathan cross was helped along from right to left by Adeyemo before it reached the feet of Cleary, who rifled home a rasping shot.

Aldershot had spent very little time in the ascendency but did muster a brief flicker after going 2-0 down. Hakeem Sandah jinked his way down the left before cutting in to pull the trigger, although his powerful drive was straight down the throat of Cieran Slicker.

Barnsley soon returned to the front foot and did not wait long before striking for a third time. Connell split the Shots defence with an incisive pass latched on to by Yoganathan, who kept his cool to slot past Hayes.

The visitors enjoyed their best spell late in the first half, knitting together some neat passes to emerge from their camped-in state and ask questions of the hosts. Dominic Odusanya stung the palms of Slicker and Sandah then forced the goalleeper to tip a dipping shot behind at full stretch.

However, the fourth goal of the game, on the stroke of half-time, was registered by Barnsley. Aldershot failed to deal with a Larkeche cross that made its way to Yoganathan, who steered home his second of the afternoon.

Makenzie Kirk replaced Tobi Adeyemo at the interval and was presented with a glorious opportunity less than five minutes into the second half. He found himself on the end of a slick move but Hayes produced an impressive save to thwart the on-loan Portsmouth man.

Aldershot struggled to clear their lines in the aftermath and Kirk should have had a second bite of the cherry, but McGeehan elected to shoot when a pass to the forward was a better option.

With Barnsley cruising, there was no urgent need for McGeehan to make amends, yet he did so regardless as he tapped home a fifth on the rebound after Kirk was denied.

Aldershot’s defensive door continued to creak open and Barnsley refused to relent in their pursuit of goals. McGeehan completed his hat-trick just five minutes after his second, striking low and hard after connecting with a Connell pass.

The visitors were well-backed and finally gave their supporters something to celebrate late on, when Lewis slipped in behind the Barnsley backline and tucked the ball away in the bottom corner.

Lewis found the target again in similar circumstances with four minutes of normal timne remaining, although it was not the final goal of the afternoon. Barnsley bit back immediately via substitute Brownlie, who tidly swept past Hayes to make it 7-2.

#1900. Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho addresses Vinicius Junior's struggles at Bernabeu

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 13:41, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 13:44

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho remains confident that Vinicius Junior will rediscover his top form for the Spanish giants in the not too distant future.

Vinicius will complete a four-game domestic suspension on Saturday, when Real Madrid continue their La Liga campaign against Valencia.

The 26-year-old has had a tough campaign to date, only managing one goal and three assists in 12 appearances for Los Blancos in all competitions.

Vinicius again struggled to make his mark against AEK Athens in the Champions League, with the statistics showing how difficult a game it was for the Brazilian.

The attacker will once again be available in La Liga after the November international break, and Mourinho has said that he will continue to help Vinicius rediscover his best form.

“For me, the most important thing is the team. Never by my own will would I harm the team to benefit a player. When we return to normal with Vini Jr. being available, I’ll manage it," Mourinho told reporters during Friday's press conference.

"I want the team to think game by game, but as a coach, I have to think about the next matches and the sequence of games we have. The match against AEK was for Vini Jr., to give some rest to a player like [Arda] Guler, who had some issues.

“The most straightforward answer to your question is that a coach must do everything to have his players at the highest level, try different strategies, in-game or personal management, and always believe in the player’s true potential.

"A bad player will always be bad no matter how much you try to improve them. A good one has their bad moments but leaves the door open to return to their normal state.

"The game that Vini Jr. played in Athens - if it wasn’t Vini Jr. but a regular player - we’d all say he had a good game. Not incredible because his team didn’t play incredibly.

"We always expect the Vini Jr. who eliminated me from the Champions League, and that version exists, which we all expect. We must continue working with all strategies at all levels.

"Something important is the friendship of his teammates, without exception. When deciding who plays, the team is above the individual.”

The South American has scored 129 goals and registered 103 assists in 387 matches for Real Madrid during a highly-successful period.

Vinicius had been heavily linked with a move to Arsenal during the summer transfer window before ultimately signing a new long-term contract at Bernabeu.

#1896. Martin O'Neill's greatest mistake was staying after winning the league

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:24 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 14:51 EDT, 3 November 2026

Winning the league title in such dramatic fashion on the final day of last season, Martin O’Neill should have recognised the moment for what it was. The End.

In a chaotic season where he had rescued Celtic from oblivion not once but twice, that was the moment when the credits should have rolled.

The blockbuster Hollywood finale. The perfect opportunity to go out in a blaze of glory and sail off into the sunset, his legacy not only secure but further enhanced.

His decision to stay on as manager this season has proven to be a mistake. In his heart of hearts, O’Neill must realise this. The whole thing is done. Finished. Finito. Terminado, as one of his predecessors would have said.

On the back of the 2-0 defeat to Falkirk last weekend, it has now reached the point where O’Neill’s continued presence at the club is damaging his legacy.

The fans are turning on him. They don’t care what he did for the club 20-odd years ago. They aren’t interested in his wisecracks. They don’t want to hear nostalgic tales of old about how things used to be.

They care only about the here and now and about what they are watching on the pitch. Now mired in a run of three wins in their last ten matches, O’Neill’s side are, if anything, actually getting worse.

O’Neill’s argument about still being top of the league is one of deflection, denial and delusion. Complete and utter claptrap. It is an insult to the intelligence of Celtic supporters.

Martin O'Neill's Celtic team lead the table but have struggled to convince

This is the problem. If there is solid evidence to support the claims that he has lost the faith of the players, then he is also rapidly losing the faith of the fans.

In a way, it is sad that it should come to this. The man is 74 years old. He didn’t ask to be thrust back into the spotlight. At least, not initially.

On two occasions, he answered an SOS call from Dermot Desmond last season. He came back and he did exactly what was asked of him.

If Celtic had any sort of competent succession plan in place, there wouldn’t even have been a conversation around O’Neill’s future towards the end of last season.

It would have been a case of shaking his hand, thanking him enormously for a heroic contribution, before being serenaded by supporters one last time after winning a league and cup double.

Yet, going back to those final few weeks of last season, it was clear O’Neill had the bug for it once again. He was never going to walk away, and nor were the board ever going to turn him down.

In the end, the situation needed one of two things to happen. It either needed O’Neill to save himself from his own desires, and have some sense and foresight about how the club was being run, or it needed Celtic to show some vision and make a proper long-term appointment.

In the absence of both, it was the blind leading the blind. O’Neill hung around primarily to have another crack at Europe, the Celtic board thought they had a bulletproof shield by retaining the services of a club icon.

The argument that kept on being trotted out at the time centred on how winning the league title meant that O’Neill had earned the right to stay on.

But that fundamentally missed the point. Of course he had earned the right. He’s Martin O’Neill. Only Jock Stein stands above him in the pantheon of the club’s all-time greatest managers.

Fans adored him (yes, past tense). But just because he had earned the right doesn’t mean it was the right thing to do. That’s the key difference.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill lifts the league trophy back in May

Whenever Manchester United inevitably sack Michael Carrick, let’s suppose for a second that Sir Alex Ferguson comes in and takes charge for a few games.

Everything goes well, the team start winning games again, everyone starts getting those old feelings coming back.

But would it mean that the right thing to do is to hand Sir Alex the job for another season? Of course it wouldn’t.

The failure to separate that nostalgia and love for O’Neill from what was required moving into this season was a catastrophic error of judgment on Celtic’s part.

The club had absolutely no idea how to move forward in the summer – just like they would have absolutely no idea who to appoint now if O’Neill was to be relieved of his duties.

In the past, Celtic sacked Tommy Burns. They sacked Billy McNeill. The belief that O’Neill could not suffer a similar fate is hugely naive.

Right now, a growing section of the fanbase view him as little more than an extension of Desmond. His status as a club icon is fading.

Over the weekend, a couple of articles surfaced from a few years ago when O’Neill was sacked as Nottingham Forest manager in 2019.

They spoke of how O’Neill eventually lost the dressing room and of how the players were left bemused by his lack of detail on the tactical side of the game.

Some Celtic fans view O'Neill as little more than an extension of major shareholder Dermot Desmond

The parallels with this current Celtic side are obvious. Just look at the comments from Callum McGregor and Cameron Carter-Vickers over recent weeks.

They are a team with absolutely no tactical identity – and it’s difficult to see how this gets any better for as long as O’Neill, along with coaches Shaun Maloney and Mark Fotheringham, remain at the helm.

O’Neill attended a Q&A session at a supporter’s club in Greenock on Monday night, along with chief executive Michael Nicholson and chairman Brian Wilson.

A bizarre announcement from Celtic yesterday claimed that the questioning had been ‘hard but fair’ as supporters voiced their concerns about the current malaise.

The one man who continues to dodge the Paxman treatment is, of course, Desmond himself, the club’s largest shareholder who operates as the commander-in-chief.

And the one question which is now becoming painfully unavoidable is this: what grounds are there for Martin O’Neill to continue as Celtic manager?

JJ Gabriel has revealed the key motivation behind his impending move to Real Madrid after turning his back on Manchester United.

Gabriel, who turned 16 on October 6, informed United of his desire to leave in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, but has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

And in a brief interview with the Spanish outlet Marca, Gabriel revealed he has one particular goal in mind for his time at Real.

A move to Real is a bold step at such a young age, and United legend Ryan Giggs believes Gabriel may have been better served following the example of Max Dowman, whose development is not being rushed by Arsenal or Mikel Arteta.

‘So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track,’ Giggs said of Gabriel on Rio Ferdinand Presents.

‘I trained at 15, I didn’t play for the first team until two years later so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment.

‘And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different. That first game, yeah, you might do alright, but you have to do it for 40, 50 games a season. You’re going to get injuries, loss of form, bad results, so you have to be patient.

‘If you’re on the right trajectory then just bide your time, no matter how good you are.

‘Max Dowman is unbelievable but he’s not playing for Arsenal at the moment.

‘I’m sure he’ll bide his time, I’m sure he’s getting impatient, but he’s not kicking off, he knows in a couple of years time he might be the main man for Arsenal.’

#1892. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta issues reassuring Ezri Konsa injury update before Hull City

By Ben Knapton | 06 Nov 2026 13:54, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 14:03

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has provided a reassuring injury update on Ezri Konsa ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash against Hull City.

The England international was taken off with 62 minutes gone against Slavia Prague in midweek, and Arteta revealed after the game that he was dealing with "some issues".

However, Konsa was named in the England squad for the upcoming November international break, suggesting that the unspecified problem he was dealing with against Slavia Prague was not serious.

Konsa was also spotted in team training earlier on Friday, and speaking to reporters in his pre-game press conference, Arteta alleviated fears over an injury to the centre-back.

"He is fine," Arteta said. "He was feeling much better today. We took him out as a precaution [against Slavia Prague] but yesterday and today he is feeling good."

Nevertheless, Arsenal can afford to play it safe with Konsa thanks to the presence of Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba, the latter of whom made a matchday squad for the first time this season in Prague.

The Frenchman was an unused substitute following four months out with a back injury, though, and Arteta also revealed that the Gunners have been in close contact with France ahead of their international squad announcement later on Friday.

While Saliba is back in the ranks, Arteta has conceded that Bukayo Saka will need "weeks" to recover from quadriceps damage, suggesting that a comeback before December is unlikely.

"No, we talk about weeks... let's see after international break," Arteta added. "He's going to start hitting the pitch and start, actually have more activities, how he feels. But, unfortunately, he's going to be out for a while.

"I don't want to push these guys into too much pressure. They are doing their best to get him in shape. Bukayo is desperate to get back with the team, but it's still quite early."

Even though Konsa has been declared fit by Arteta, the Englishman's recent blow may have left the door ajar for Saliba to come straight back into the Arsenal ranks.

The 25-year-old is evidently capable of playing some minutes for the Gunners, hence his involvement in the matchday squad in midweek, but just how many minutes is another question entirely.

Given Saliba did not come off the bench in the Czech Republic, Arteta may see fit to introduce him as a substitute, which would also allow him to enjoy a proper reception on his comeback appearance.

Therefore, if Arteta does decide to err on the side of caution with Konsa, Mosquera should be first in line to join Gabriel Magalhaes in defence.

#1886. Hearts vs Falkirk - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 06 Nov 2026 13:56, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 14:02

Meeting for the second time in less than two months, Falkirk travel to the Scottish capital looking to extend their winning run to five matches when they take on an inconsistent Hearts side.

The Jambos were in European action during the week but suffered their second defeat in five days, losing 3-1 to Thun in Switzerland, while the Bairns secured a memorable victory over Celtic to claim their first win against the Glasgow giants in 19 years.

After narrowly missing out on their first Scottish Premiership title since 1960, Hearts entered the summer facing a significant rebuilding task, having come closer than any club outside Celtic and Rangers to winning the championship since 1985.

Their preparations were further complicated when manager Derek McInnes departed to take charge the Gers, bringing several key players with him.

Wouter Vrancken was appointed as the new Jambos head coach in June, becoming the first Belgian to take charge of the club, but he has so far been unable to maintain the momentum built under McInnes.

After 23 matches, the former Sint-Truidense manager has recorded just eight victories, alongside six draws and nine defeats, leaving Hearts third in the Scottish Premiership, out of the Scottish League Cup and 32nd in the Conference League league-phase table.

Hearts travelled to Thun on the back of Sunday's Scottish League Cup semi-final defeat to city rivals Hibernian, meaning Vrancken's men were in need of a positive result to lift the mood around the club.

However, a poor defensive display saw the Jambos suffer a 3-1 defeat against their Swiss opponents, leaving them without a victory in the Conference League after three matches, having also drawn with Nordsjaelland and lost to Trabzonspor in their previous European outings.

As for visiting Falkirk, they make the short journey east in considerably better spirits after securing a memorable victory over league leaders Celtic last weekend, courtesy of first-half goals from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser.

The victory at the Falkirk Stadium was their first against the Bhoys in almost two decades and continued an impressive run of form following their difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign.

John McGlynn's side have now won four consecutive Scottish Premiership matches, a run that began in mid-October following a defeat to Dundee, and have climbed the table from second-bottom to fourth.

Their impressive turnaround has also been built on improved defensive performances, with only two sides in the division conceding fewer than their 12 goals, while only Rangers have collected more points across the last six Premiership matchweeks.

Bairns' superb run has also earned manager McGlynn the Premiership Manager of the Month award for October, and his side will now look to overcome a Hearts team they have already beaten this season, having secured a 2-1 victory in September.

Despite their inconsistent performances and recurring defensive issues, Hearts have also been hampered by a significant injury list during the opening months of the season.

An injury-hit squad travelled to Switzerland in midweek and returned with further concerns after Stephen Kingsley was forced off shortly after the hour mark against Thun, ruling him out of Sunday's encounter alongside 10 other players.

Harry Milne, Calvin Miller and Blair Spittal are among those currently sidelined, with Milne not expected to return to action until August 2027.

As for the visitors, Falkirk also head into the weekend with a large number of players unavailable through injury.

Despite the joy following their victory over Celtic, Ryan Strain was forced off in the early stages of that match and will play no part this weekend.

He joins Leon McCann, Aodhan Doherty, Joseph Gardner, Ethan Laidlaw, Keelan Adams and Aidan Nesbitt in the treatment room.

Reus; Gillies, Fagan-Walcott, Findlay, McCart; Kerjota, Altena, Mendy, McPake; Guendouz, C. Braga

Bain; Allan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Melniks, Spencer; Ross, Barbrook, Earnes; Murrell

Despite arriving in Edinburgh in contrasting form, the two sides are relatively evenly matched in the league table, and we expect Falkirk to provide a stern test for their hosts.

Hearts will be keen to respond after successive defeats, but with McGlynn's men enjoying an excellent run of results, we anticipate a closely contested encounter with the points ultimately being shared.
